summary: Proposes a Mail Box Protocol, a standard way for a site to receive sequential files for immediate or deferred printing or other uses. A sending program would send the file with optional control codes. It does not decide how the site stores or prints the file. It was replaced by RFC 221.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 196 proposes numbered mail boxes for delivering files to remote sites. The site decides whether to print, store, or otherwise handle the file.

subtitle: A proposal for sending sequential files to a site's network mailbox.

tldr.problem: A sender needed a standard way to deliver files to a remote site's printing or processing service without knowing its local file-system commands.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 196 proposes numbered mail boxes that receive sequential files, with optional control codes for mail-box number, transmission type, and printer settings.
tldr.outcome: The proposal leaves handling and storage details to each site and was later obsoleted by RFC 221.

today: RFC 196 was obsoleted by RFC 221. It is an early proposal for delivering files to remote sites through numbered mail boxes.

sections.title: A Mail Box for Remote Files
sections.content: The Mail Box Protocol aims to provide a standard way for sites to receive sequential files for immediate or deferred printing or other uses. Its motivation includes the Network Information Center's need to send documents to remote sites and receive documents without learning each site's file-system conventions.
sections.plainLanguage: A sender can deliver a file to a numbered mail box at another site. The receiving site decides what to do with the file.

sections.title: Text Format and Control Codes
sections.content: The default transmission is 7-bit ASCII in 8-bit bytes, with the high-order bit set to zero. Mail box 0 assumes a printer with lines 72 characters wide and pages of 66 lines. Optional control codes can select a mail box, transmission code type, line width, or page size.
sections.plainLanguage: The default mailbox assumes text for a printer and provides basic page settings. A sender can include control codes to choose another mail box or printing format.

sections.title: Connection and Site Responsibilities
sections.content: The protocol uses the Network Control Program, Initial Connection Protocol, and Data Transfer Protocol. The note identifies socket 5 as a candidate for a standard mail-box connection, not as a finalized assignment. Each site remains responsible for how it stores, handles, or prints received files.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal uses existing network connection and transfer conventions. It does not dictate how a site stores or prints the files it receives.
